title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
slides: Why did Meta quietly delete that language?
Its AI terms warned users about scraping and training
But the removed clause is about something narrower
Your public posts may train future Meta models
Audit your privacy settings before the next update
thread_text:
1. Meta quietly deleted a clause

Its AI terms had warned users about scraping and training. That warning is now gone, and the reason isn't obvious.

2. The removed clause was narrower

It didn't cover all scraping or all training. It targeted a specific case Meta no longer wants to mention.

3. Your public posts train future models

Anything you've posted publicly can end up in training data. Meta's own terms say so — for now.

4. The deletion changes the deal

If the clause is gone, the rules you agreed to may no longer apply. The silence is the signal.

5. Audit your privacy settings now

Open your settings and check what's public before the next update. What would you change if you knew it was training data?

instagram.caption:
Meta removed a clause from its AI terms that specifically warned users about scraping and data training.

The warning covered a narrower case than it seemed — but now it's gone, and Meta hasn't explained why. 👀

What remains is this: your public posts can still end up in training data for future models.

If you publish anything publicly, the terms you originally agreed to may no longer say what they said. 📄

Open your privacy settings now and check what's public before the next update. 🔍 Would you change anything if you knew it was training data?
